# Feature: Checkpoint tile — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #48 (Checkpoint tile) from Terrain and Hazards before it is used in real levels. Effect: Step on it and later hazards return you here with the timer intact. Unique: a respawn you set by touch, with the timer still running. Useful: retry a lethal room from inside the attempt, not from the start. Source status in the candidate file is 'revised'; it was revised from human review and is now treated as a trial candidate.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** step on it and later hazards return you here with the timer intact.

**So that** retry a lethal room from inside the attempt, not from the start.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Checkpoint tile for the first time in its teaching room (mech-48-checkpoint-tile-room). Teaching moment: First room: a checkpoint tile just before a hazard corridor, placed slightly off the direct line. A player who runs the direct line and dies in the corridor is returned to the level start instead of the tile they passed, which teaches that a checkpoint only counts once it has been stepped on. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Stepping on it lights it and makes it your respawn
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Any hazard or enemy death after that returns you to the last checkpoint you touched instead of restarting, with the timer still running and your orbs and keys as they were at the death
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Multiple checkpoints: the last one touched is active

## Edge Cases & Rules

- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.
- No soft-lock: every reachable state has a legal move, a lose, or a reset.
- Definition audit: checkpoint: respawn set by touch, defined here; only the last one touched is active, and hazard deaths return to it with the timer running
- Definition audit: hazard: any tile whose entry loses the attempt, for example fire per mechanic 43 or lava per mechanic 44 in this file; with an active checkpoint the loss returns here instead of restarting
- Definition audit: timer: the level countdown, which keeps running through a checkpoint return and is cleared only by a manual restart

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Checkpoint tile's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Testing

Needs a mechanics playground: new — Test Level mech-48-checkpoint-tile-room, built from this mechanic's teaching moment above. What to check there: every rule in Player-Facing Behavior, played in mech-48-checkpoint-tile-room; the teaching moment's first (naive) action should fail as described and the corrected action should succeed. Record play sessions for replay: yes — sessions are the review evidence. Synergy rooms are explicitly deferred to a later run and are not part of this feature's check.
Named test cases (from the candidate file; all must be played):
- Test case touch activates, death returns there: stepping on the tile lights it, and a later hazard death returns the player to it with timer, orbs and keys as at the death
- Test case last one touched wins: touching a second checkpoint moves the respawn to it and unlights the first; deaths then return to the second
- Test case adversarial skip the checkpoint: running the direct line past the tile and dying returns the player to the level start, exactly as the teaching moment promises
- Test case restart and replay: restart clears every active checkpoint, and a recorded death-and-return session replays to the same end state
